question: Find all real values of $k$ for which $(k-1)x+2y=3$ and $3x+(k+1)y=4$ form a consistent system with a unique solution.
explanation:
Coefficient determinant
$$D= egin{vmatrix}k-1&2\3&k+1\end{vmatrix}=(k-1)(k+1)-6=k^2-7$$
Unique-solution condition
The system is consistent with a unique solution when $$D e0$$
Restriction on $k$
Thus, $$k^2-7 e0$$ which gives $$k e\sqrt{7}\quad ext{and}\quad k e-\sqrt{7}$$
Hence, the system has a unique solution for $$k\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{-\sqrt{7},\sqrt{7}\}$$
